_help: Searchable command reference on /cli. Taken from the CLI README and docs/commands.md (version 2.2.0, agent from 3.0). group order = display order. sudo: true when the command needs root.

groups.title: Health
groups.note: No console and no sudo needed.

commands.text: One line per running or failed service: state, uptime, listening ports, health. Application services first, then system services. Exit code 3 when a service is Failed or Restarting.
One service in detail: type, state, health, uptime, restarts, main PID, unit file, ports, errors and warnings in the last 24 hours.
Live status view, refreshed every 5 seconds. Ctrl+C to stop.
Every loaded service as JSON, with the unit file path and category. --logs adds a log summary per service.
Print the version. --json prints one line for the console: version, OS, architecture, server, system id, registration and service account (never a key).
Show every command. The man page: man atglance.
Save the console URL and your personal API key (atgla-). The key comes from a hidden prompt, stdin or ATGLANCE_TOKEN, never from an argument.
The console user, organisation, key name and expiry of the saved key.
Check the whole setup: settings, console, token, clock, system, systemd, journal, queue, key expiry and schedule. Alias: doctor.
Forget the saved key. The system identity stays.
Register this server with the console. The server makes its own system key and keeps it in /var/lib/atglance/identity.json (0600).
The system as the console sees it: id, name, status, workspace, registered at.
Set the system inactive. Backups are refused until it is reactivated. --force uses an admin's email and password or PIN.
Set the system active again.
Replace the system key.
Change the service account key (atgsa-) used for scheduled runs. The system keeps its id, key and history.
For consoles that install the CLI over SSH or WinRM: reads one JSON object on stdin with the console URL, system identity and service account key. Never prints a key.
Send queued backups, then back up every running or failed service whose unit file changed. Unchanged files are skipped.
Upload the unit file of one service or of all services. Queued when the console cannot be reached.
The versions the console holds: id, version, created, by.
Download a version to /var/lib/atglance/pulled/<service>/. Changes nothing else.
Unified diff of a version against the live unit file. Exit 0 identical, 3 different.
Show the diff, confirm, back up the live file, write, reload systemd, restart and wait until stable. Rolls back if the restart fails.
Write /etc/cron.d/atglance: a daily check around 06:00 and a daily sync between 02:00 and 03:59, at random minutes.
Remove the cron jobs.
The job times and the last log lines (journalctl -t atglance).
The organisation's security log, newest first: failed, successful and locked force actions.
Accounts whose force actions are locked, with the time the lock ends.

groups.title: Agent (3.0)
groups.note: Outbound encrypted connection to the console, no open ports. Linux, Windows Server and macOS.

commands.text: Install or remove the agent as a system service.
Control the agent service.
Connection state of the agent.
Run the agent in the foreground.
Show or follow the agent log.
